title: STILL PRESENT (r3): wrong-person awaiting UPDATE still unguarded on taken_over_at — guarded SQL unwired, race pin vacuous
evidence:
form_handler.gleam:1235-1252: "case row.taken_over_at != "" { True -> wisp.redirect(to: "/reference/" <> token) False -> ... case row.correction_cycles >= 1 { True -> exhaust_wrong_person(...) False -> case sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated)" — update_reference_call_status.sql:22-23: "WHERE id = $1
  AND status = $5::reference_call_status" (no taken_over_at clause; take-over writes only taken_over_at + next_attempt_at, status stays contact_initiated). Test wrong_person_awaiting_sql_has_taken_over_backstop_test (reference_checks_actions_integration_test.gleam:1729-1762) calls "rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)" DIRECTLY — never the POST route.
detail: The executed awaiting transition is still update_reference_call_status, whose status-only guard matches a taken-over row (take-over keeps contact_initiated). The read-time check closes only pre-read take-overs; the read→UPDATE window stays open. The race pin calls the guarded SQL directly while the handler uses a different UPDATE — neutralizing the backstop does not turn it red. Both mandate conditions unmet.
recommended_fix: Wire mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person into apply_wrong_person's awaiting branch; add an integration test driving handle_wrong_person_post that races a take-over and turns red when the backstop is neutralized.
